questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: When a block of mass $M$ is suspended by a long wire of length $L$, the length of wire becomes $(L + l)$. The elastic potential energy stored in the extended wire is:
questions.explanation: $U = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Force} \times \text{Extension} = \frac{1}{2} M g l$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A mass $m$ is attached to a thin wire and whirled in a vertical circle. The wire is most likely to break when:
questions.optionA: The mass is at the highest point
questions.optionC: The mass is at the lowest point
questions.optionD: Inclined at an angle of $60^\circ$ from vertical
questions.explanation: Tension is maximum at the lowest point: $T_{\text{bottom}} = \frac{m v^2}{r} + m g$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Ionized hydrogen atoms ($p$) and $\alpha$-particles with same momenta enter perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The ratio of their orbital radii $r_H : r_\alpha$ is:
questions.explanation: $r = \frac{p}{q B} \propto \frac{1}{q} \implies \frac{r_H}{r_\alpha} = \frac{q_\alpha}{q_H} = \frac{2e}{e} = 2 : 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Body A of mass $4m$ moving with speed $u$ collides head-on elastically with stationary body B of mass $2m$. The fraction of energy lost by body A is:
questions.explanation: $v_1 = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2} u = \frac{4m - 2m}{4m + 2m} u = \frac{1}{3} u$. $\text{Fraction remaining} = (1/3)^2 = 1/9 \implies \text{Fraction lost} = 1 - 1/9 = 8/9$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In YDSE with light $400\text{ nm}$, angular width of first minima is $0.2^\circ$. What will be angular width if entire apparatus is immersed in water ($\mu = 4/3$)?
questions.explanation: $\theta' = \frac{\theta}{\mu} = \frac{0.2^\circ}{4/3} = 0.15^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In which of the following devices, the eddy current effect is NOT used / desirable?
questions.explanation: Electric heaters and electromagnets use Joule heating / magnetic flux rather than eddy currents (Official answer key accepts 3 & 4).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A soap bubble radius $1\text{ mm}$ is blown from solution ($T = 2.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ N/m}$). Excess pressure inside equals pressure at depth $Z_0$ of water. Value of $Z_0$ is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $\Delta P = \frac{4T}{R} = \frac{4 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-2}}{10^{-3}} = 100\text{ N/m}^2$. $\rho g Z_0 = 100 \implies 1000 \times 10 \times Z_0 = 100 \implies Z_0 = 0.01\text{ m} = 1\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Which colour of visible light has the LONGEST wavelength in vacuum?
questions.explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength ($\sim 700\text{ nm}$) and violet has the shortest ($\sim 400\text{ nm}$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A disc of radius $2\text{ m}$ and mass $100\text{ kg}$ rolls on horizontal floor at $v = 20\text{ cm/s} = 0.2\text{ m/s}$. Work needed to stop it is:
questions.explanation: $W = \text{Total KE} = \frac{1}{2} M v^2 \left(1 + \frac{k^2}{R^2}\right) = \frac{3}{4} M v^2 = \frac{3}{4} (100) (0.2)^2 = 3\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Displacement of particle is $y = A_0 + A\sin\omega t + B\cos\omega t$. The amplitude of its oscillation is:
questions.explanation: $A_0$ represents a constant baseline shift. Resultant oscillation amplitude is $\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two thin equi-convex lenses ($f$) in contact have combination focal length $F_1$. When space between them is filled with glycerin ($\mu = 1.5$), equivalent focal length is $F_2$. Ratio $F_1 : F_2$ is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{F_1} = \frac{2}{f} \implies F_1 = \frac{f}{2}$. Glycerin forms concave lens of power $-1/f \implies \frac{1}{F_2} = \frac{2}{f} - \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{f} \implies F_2 = f$. Ratio $F_1 : F_2 = 1 : 2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a rigid closed container leads to:
questions.optionB: Increase in its kinetic energy ($E \propto T$)
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to absolute temperature: $KE = \frac{3}{2} k_B T$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An electron accelerated through potential difference $10000\text{ V}$ has de Broglie wavelength nearly:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A copper rod of $88\text{ cm}$ ($\alpha_{\text{Cu}} = 1.7 \times 10^{-5}$) and aluminium rod of unknown length have difference in length independent of temperature. Length of aluminium rod is ($\alpha_{\text{Al}} = 2.2 \times 10^{-5}$):
questions.explanation: $L_{\text{Cu}} \alpha_{\text{Cu}} = L_{\text{Al}} \alpha_{\text{Al}} \implies L_{\text{Al}} = \frac{88 \times 1.7 \times 10^{-5}}{2.2 \times 10^{-5}} = 68\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Pick the WRONG statement in the context of rainbow:
questions.optionA: When light undergoes two internal reflections in water drop, secondary rainbow forms
questions.optionB: Order of colours is reversed in secondary rainbow
questions.optionC: An observer can see a rainbow when his front is towards the sun (Sun must be behind observer)
questions.optionD: Rainbow is combined effect of dispersion, refraction and reflection
questions.explanation: To observe a rainbow, the sun must be behind the observer and water droplets in front.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A body weighs $200\text{ N}$ on Earth surface. How much will it weigh halfway down to the centre of Earth ($d = R/2$)?
questions.explanation: $g' = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right) = g(1 - 0.5) = \frac{g}{2} \implies W' = \frac{200}{2} = 100\text{ N}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Six similar bulbs are connected across DC source $E$. Ratio of power consumption when (i) all 6 are glowing and (ii) two from A and one from B are glowing is:
questions.explanation: In case (i), $R_{\text{eq1}} = R/3 + R/3 = 2R/3 \implies P_1 = \frac{3E^2}{2R}$. In case (ii), $R_{\text{eq2}} = R/2 + R = 3R/2 \implies P_2 = \frac{2E^2}{3R}$. Ratio $P_1 / P_2 = 9 : 4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a p-type semiconductor, which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.optionA: Electrons are majority carriers and trivalent atoms are dopants
questions.optionB: Holes are majority carriers and trivalent atoms are dopants
questions.optionC: Holes are majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are dopants
questions.optionD: Electrons are majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are dopants
questions.explanation: Doping tetravalent Si with trivalent atoms (B, Al, Ga) creates holes as majority carriers in p-type semiconductors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Average velocity of a particle executing simple harmonic motion in ONE complete cycle is:
questions.explanation: Net displacement in one complete cycle is zero, so average velocity is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The SI unit of thermal conductivity $K$ is:
questions.explanation: $K = \frac{Q d}{A \Delta T t} = \frac{\text{W} \cdot \text{m}}{\text{m}^2 \cdot \text{K}} = \text{W m}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A solid cylinder of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $4\text{ cm}$ rotates at $3\text{ rpm}$. Torque required to stop it after $2\pi\text{ revolutions}$ is:
questions.explanation: $I = \frac{1}{2} M R^2 = 1.6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^2$. $\omega_0 = 3 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 0.1\pi\text{ rad/s}$. $\alpha = \frac{\omega_0^2}{2\theta} = \frac{0.01\pi^2}{2(4\pi^2)} = 1.25 \times 10^{-3} \implies \tau = I\alpha = 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ N m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A force $F = 20 + 10y$ acts on a particle in $y$-direction. Work done to move particle from $y=0$ to $y=1\text{ m}$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Which of the following acts as a circuit protection / safety device?
questions.explanation: A fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit during overcurrent or short circuit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In the two circuits shown with ideal voltmeters and ammeters across identical $10\,\Omega$ resistors and $10\text{ V}$ sources:
questions.explanation: Ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance and ideal ammeter has zero resistance, so both circuits read $V_1 = V_2 = 10\text{ V}$ and $i_1 = i_2 = 1\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A hollow metal sphere of radius $R$ is uniformly charged. The electric field due to sphere at distance $r$ from centre is:
questions.optionA: Increases as $r$ increases for $r < R$ and for $r > R$
questions.optionB: Zero as $r$ increases for $r < R$, decreases as $r$ increases for $r > R$
questions.optionC: Zero as $r$ increases for $r < R$, increases as $r$ increases for $r > R$
questions.explanation: $E = 0$ inside a conducting hollow sphere ($r < R$) and $E = \frac{k Q}{r^2} \propto 1/r^2$ outside ($r > R$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: At point A, angle of dip is $\delta = +25^\circ$. At point B, dip is $\delta = -25^\circ$. We can interpret that:
questions.optionA: A and B are both in northern hemisphere
questions.optionB: A is in southern and B is in northern hemisphere
questions.optionC: A is in northern hemisphere and B is in southern hemisphere
questions.optionD: A and B are both in southern hemisphere
questions.explanation: Positive dip angle corresponds to the Northern hemisphere; negative dip angle corresponds to the Southern hemisphere.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Total energy of electron in hydrogen orbit is $-3.4\text{ eV}$. Its kinetic and potential energies are respectively:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In total internal reflection when angle of incidence equals critical angle ($i = C$), angle of refraction is:
questions.explanation: At critical angle, refracted ray grazes the boundary with angle of refraction $r = 90^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Work done to raise a mass $m$ from Earth's surface to height $h = R$ is:
questions.explanation: $W = \Delta U = \frac{m g h}{1 + h/R} = \frac{m g R}{1 + 1} = \frac{1}{2} m g R$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: When object is shot up incline of $60^\circ$, it travels distance $x_1$. When shot with same speed up $30^\circ$ incline, distance is $x_2$. Ratio $x_1 : x_2$ is:
questions.explanation: $x = \frac{u^2}{2g\sin\theta} \propto \frac{1}{\sin\theta} \implies \frac{x_1}{x_2} = \frac{\sin 30^\circ}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2} = 1 : \sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An $\alpha$-particle consists of:
questions.explanation: An $\alpha$-particle is a doubly ionized helium nucleus ($^4_2\text{He}^{2+}$) composed of 2 protons and 2 neutrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Swimmer speed in still water is $20\text{ m/s}$. River speed is $10\text{ m/s}$ flowing East. To cross river along shortest path, stroke angle w.r.t. North is:
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta = \frac{v_r}{v_s} = \frac{10}{20} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = 30^\circ\text{ West of North}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A particle moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ is acted upon by 3 forces forming a closed cyclic vector triangle PQR. Velocity of particle will:
questions.explanation: For closed vector polygon, resultant force $\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = 0 \implies \vec{a} = 0$, so velocity remains constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two particles A and B move in concentric circles $r_A$ and $r_B$ with same time period $T$. Ratio of their angular speeds $\omega_A : \omega_B$ is:
questions.explanation: $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$. Since time periods are equal, $\omega_A = \omega_B \implies 1 : 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $10\text{ kg}$ block is pressed against inner vertical wall of rotating cylinder of radius $1\text{ m}$ ($\mu = 0.1$). Minimum angular velocity to prevent slipping is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $\mu N = m g \implies \mu (m r \omega^2) = m g \implies \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu r}} = \sqrt{\frac{10}{0.1 \times 1}} = 10\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two parallel infinite line charges with $+\lambda$ and $-\lambda$ are separated by distance $2R$. Electric field midway between them is:
questions.explanation: $E = E_+ + E_- = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} + \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} = \frac{\lambda}{\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$ towards the negative line charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Point charges $+Q$ and $-Q$ exert force $F$. If $25\%$ charge of A is transferred to B, force between them becomes:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A small hole of area $2\text{ mm}^2$ near bottom of tank of height $2\text{ m}$. Rate of flow of water is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{40} = 6.32\text{ m/s}$. Flow rate $Q = A v = (2 \times 10^{-6}) \times 6.32 = 12.64 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3/\text{s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The Boolean logic operation performed by the circuit diagram with parallel switches A, B connected across LED (Y) is:
questions.explanation: LED turns OFF only when BOTH switches A and B are closed (conducting to ground), which is the truth table of NAND gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: In which thermodynamic process is heat NEITHER absorbed NOR released by a system?
questions.explanation: In an adiabatic process, there is zero heat transfer between system and surroundings ($dQ = 0$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An 800 turn coil of area $0.05\text{ m}^2$ in field $5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$ is rotated by $90^\circ$ in $0.1\text{ s}$. Induced EMF is:
questions.explanation: $\varepsilon = \frac{N A B}{t} = \frac{800 \times 0.05 \times (5 \times 10^{-5})}{0.1} = 0.02\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Radius of circle is $3\text{ m}$, period $T = 4\text{ s}$, clockwise rotation starting at top $(0,3)$. $y$-projection of rotating particle is:
questions.explanation: $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{\pi}{2}\text{ rad/s}$. At $t=0$, $y = +3\text{ m} \implies y(t) = 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A $20\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is charged at $dV/dt = 3\text{ V/s}$. Conduction current in wires and displacement current in capacitor plates are:
questions.explanation: $I_c = I_d = C \frac{dV}{dt} = (20 \times 10^{-6}) \times 3 = 60\,\mu\text{A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Errors in A, B, C, D are $1\%, 2\%, 3\%, 4\%$. For $X = \frac{A^2 B^{1/2}}{C^{1/3} D^3}$, maximum percentage error in $X$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carries constant current. Plot of magnetic field $B$ vs distance $d$ from centre shows:
questions.optionC: Linear increase for $d \le R$, then $1/d$ decay for $d > R$
questions.explanation: $B \propto d$ inside the wire ($d \le R$) and $B \propto 1/d$ outside the wire ($d > R$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The number of sigma ($\sigma$) and pi ($\pi$) bonds in pent-2-en-4-yne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$) is:
questions.explanation: Pent-2-en-4-yne has 1 double bond ($1\pi$) and 1 triple bond ($2\pi$) $\implies 3\pi$ bonds. Total single bonds $+ \sigma$ components $= 10\,\sigma$ bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Structure of intermediate A in industrial cumene process for manufacture of phenol is:
questions.explanation: Air oxidation of cumene (isopropylbenzene) forms cumene hydroperoxide, which rearranges in dilute acid to phenol and acetone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct structure of tribromooctaoxide ($\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$) contains terminal bromine atoms with:
questions.optionA: Three double bonded oxygens on terminal Br and two on central Br ($\text{O}_3\text{Br}-\text{BrO}_2-\text{BrO}_3$)
questions.explanation: Structure is $\text{O}_3\text{Br}-\text{BrO}_2-\text{BrO}_3$ with oxidation states $+6, +4, +6$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $4d, 5p, 5f$ and $6p$ orbitals arranged in order of DECREASING energy ($(n+l)$ rule) are:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are DISPROPORTIONATION reactions?
(a) $2\text{Cu}^+ \to \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Cu}^0$
(b) $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \to 2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$
(c) $2\text{KMnO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 + \text{MnO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
(d) $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 3\text{Mn}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \to 5\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{H}^+$
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: In (a), $\text{Cu}^+$ ($+1$) disproportionates to $+2$ and $0$. In (b), $\text{Mn}$ ($+6$) disproportionates to $+7$ and $+4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Gas at $300\text{ K}$ expands from $0.1\text{ L}$ to $0.25\text{ L}$ against constant external pressure of $2\text{ bar}$. Work done is ($1\text{ L bar} = 100\text{ J}$):
questions.explanation: $w = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V = -2(0.25 - 0.1) = -0.3\text{ L bar} = -30\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Among the following, the one that is NOT a greenhouse gas is:
questions.explanation: Major greenhouse gases are $\text{CO}_2, \text{CH}_4, \text{N}_2\text{O}, \text{O}_3$, and CFCs. $\text{SO}_2$ is a primary air pollutant / aerosol former, not a greenhouse gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For cell: $2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{I}^- \to 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{I}_2$ ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.24\text{ V}$). Standard Gibbs energy $\Delta_r G^\circ$ is ($F = 96500\text{ C/mol}$):
questions.explanation: $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ = -2 \times 96500 \times 0.24 = -46320\text{ J} = -46.32\text{ kJ/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require which alkaline earth metal cofactor?
questions.explanation: Kinase enzymes coordinating ATP require divalent $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ions as essential cofactor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Most suitable reagent for stereoselective reduction of but-2-yne to cis-but-2-ene is:
questions.explanation: Lindlar's catalyst ($\text{Pd/CaCO}_3$ poisoned with quinoline/lead) performs syn-addition yielding cis-alkenes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct thermal stability order of hydrides of Group 16 elements is:
questions.explanation: Due to decrease in $\text{E-H}$ bond dissociation energy down the group: $\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{H}_2\text{S} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{Te} > \text{H}_2\text{Po}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement?
questions.optionA: $\text{PbF}_4$ is covalent in nature ($\text{PbF}_4$ is ionic)
questions.explanation: $\text{PbF}_4$ and $\text{SnF}_4$ are ionic solids with high melting points; $\text{PbCl}_4$ is covalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Chemical Processes:
(a) Pure nitrogen, (b) Haber process, (c) Contact process, (d) Deacon's process
(i) Chlorine, (ii) Sulphuric acid, (iii) Ammonia, (iv) Thermal decomposition of Sodium azide / Barium azide
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Pure $\text{N}_2$ = Barium azide (iv), Haber = Ammonia (iii), Contact = $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (ii), Deacon = $\text{Cl}_2$ (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following diatomic species has ONLY $\pi$ bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
questions.explanation: In $\text{C}_2$, all 4 valence bonding electrons occupy degenerate $\pi_{2p}$ orbitals, so both bonds are $\pi$ bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Correct increasing order of first ionization enthalpy for second period elements is:
questions.explanation: Full $2s^2$ in Be exceeds B; half-filled $2p^3$ in N exceeds O: $\text{Li} < \text{B} < \text{Be} < \text{C} < \text{O} < \text{N} < \text{F} < \text{Ne}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a BIODEGRADABLE copolymer?
questions.explanation: Nylon-2-nylon-6 (copolymer of glycine and $\varepsilon$-amino caproic acid) is biodegradable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: pH of saturated solution of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is 9. Solubility product $K_{sp}$ of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a first order reaction, time $t$ required for $99\%$ completion is given by ($k = $ rate constant):

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a NON-ESSENTIAL amino acid synthesized in human body?
questions.explanation: Alanine is synthesized endogenously from pyruvate and is non-essential.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which reaction proceeds through an ELECTROPHILIC AROMATIC SUBSTITUTION mechanism?
questions.explanation: Chlorination of benzene with Lewis acid $\text{AlCl}_3$ generates $\text{Cl}^+$ electrophile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The binary liquid mixture that forms MAXIMUM BOILING azeotrope (negative deviation from Raoult's law) is:
questions.explanation: Water and nitric acid form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, showing large negative deviation and maximum boiling azeotrope at $120.5^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For reaction $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$, correct rate relationship is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Rate} = -\frac{d[\text{N}_2]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{d[\text{H}_2]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\text{NH}_3]}{dt}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia in Haber process is:
questions.explanation: $1\text{ N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \to 2\text{NH}_3$. Producing $20\text{ mol NH}_3$ requires $\frac{3}{2} \times 20 = 30\text{ moles of H}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds is MOST DIFFICULT to protonate?
questions.explanation: In phenol, lone pair on oxygen is delocalized into benzene ring by $+R$ resonance, making oxygen least basic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For an IDEAL SOLUTION, the correct thermodynamic condition is:
questions.optionC: $\Delta_{\text{mix}} H = 0$ at constant T and P
questions.explanation: Ideal solutions obey Raoult's law with $\Delta_{\text{mix}} H = 0$ and $\Delta_{\text{mix}} V = 0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Conjugate bases for Brönsted acids $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{HF}$ are respectively:
questions.explanation: Removing a proton ($H^+$): $\text{H}_2\text{O} - H^+ = \text{OH}^-$ and $\text{HF} - H^+ = \text{F}^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which mixture will form a NEGATIVELY charged colloidal sol $[\text{AgI}]\text{I}^-$?
questions.optionA: $50\text{ mL of } 1\text{ M AgNO}_3 + 50\text{ mL of } 1.5\text{ M KI}$
questions.optionB: $50\text{ mL of } 1\text{ M AgNO}_3 + 50\text{ mL of } 2\text{ M KI}$
questions.optionC: $50\text{ mL of } 2\text{ M AgNO}_3 + 50\text{ mL of } 1.5\text{ M KI}$
questions.optionD: $50\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M AgNO}_3 + 50\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M KI}$
questions.explanation: When $\text{KI}$ is in excess (millimoles of $\text{KI} > \text{AgNO}_3$), $\text{I}^-$ ions are preferentially adsorbed (Official key accepts 1 and 2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Among the following, the NARROW SPECTRUM antibiotic is:
questions.explanation: Penicillin G has narrow spectrum activity primarily against Gram-positive bacteria.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Alkene A on ozonolysis gives propanone and ethanal. Addition of $\text{HCl}$ to alkene A gives major product:
questions.explanation: Alkene is 2-methylbut-2-ene. Markovnikov addition of $\text{HCl}$ gives tertiary halide 2-chloro-2-methylbutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Correct $d$-electron configuration for central atom in low-spin complex $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ ($d^6$) is:
questions.explanation: $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand causing complete pairing of 6 $d$-electrons in lower $t_{2g}$ level ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement related to $\text{PCl}_5$ geometry:
questions.optionA: Three equatorial P-Cl bonds make angle of $120^\circ$
questions.optionB: Two axial P-Cl bonds make angle of $180^\circ$
questions.optionC: Axial P-Cl bonds are longer than equatorial P-Cl bonds
questions.optionD: $\text{PCl}_5$ molecule is non-reactive ($\text{PCl}_5$ is highly reactive)
questions.explanation: Due to unequal axial bond lengths and steric repulsion, $\text{PCl}_5$ is thermally unstable and reactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which mixture will make a BASIC BUFFER?
questions.optionA: $50\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M NaOH} + 25\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M CH}_3\text{COOH}$
questions.optionB: $100\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M CH}_3\text{COOH} + 100\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M NaOH}$
questions.optionC: $100\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M HCl} + 200\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M NH}_4\text{OH}$
questions.optionD: $100\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M HCl} + 100\text{ mL of } 0.1\text{ M NaOH}$
questions.explanation: $10\text{ mmol HCl} + 20\text{ mmol NH}_4\text{OH} \to 10\text{ mmol NH}_4\text{Cl} + 10\text{ mmol unreacted NH}_4\text{OH}$ (Weak base + Conjugate salt).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reaction of phthalic acid with $\text{NH}_3$ followed by strong heating gives:
questions.explanation: Heating ammonium phthalate eliminates $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ to form bicyclic phthalimide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Xenon Fluorides with Structures:
(a) $\text{XeF}_4$, (b) $\text{XeF}_6$, (c) $\text{XeOF}_4$, (d) $\text{XeO}_3$
(i) Pyramidal, (ii) Square planar, (iii) Distorted octahedral, (iv) Square pyramidal
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: $\text{XeF}_4$ = Square planar (ii), $\text{XeF}_6$ = Distorted octahedral (iii), $\text{XeOF}_4$ = Square pyramidal (iv), $\text{XeO}_3$ = Pyramidal (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Manganate ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$) and permanganate ($\text{MnO}_4^-$) ions are tetrahedral because:
questions.optionA: The $\pi$-bonding involves overlap of $p$-orbitals of oxygen with $d$-orbitals of manganese ($d_\pi-p_\pi$ bonding)
questions.optionC: Overlap of $p$-orbitals of oxygen with $p$-orbitals of manganese
questions.optionD: Overlap of $d$-orbitals of oxygen with $d$-orbitals of manganese
questions.explanation: Tetrahedral shape with multiple $\text{Mn=O}$ bonds involves $d_\pi-p_\pi$ overlapping.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following hexahalide species is NOT stable due to steric crowding?
questions.explanation: Due to small size of silicon, 6 large chloride ions cannot be accommodated around $\text{Si}^{4+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a 1-electron cell ($n=1$), $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.59\text{ V}$ at $298\text{ K}$. Equilibrium constant $K$ is ($2.303 RT/F = 0.059\text{ V}$):
questions.explanation: $E^\circ = \frac{0.059}{1} \log K \implies 0.59 = 0.059 \log K \implies \log K = 10 \implies K = 10^{10}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following Group 2 hydroxides is AMPHOTERIC in nature?
questions.explanation: $\text{Be(OH)}_2$ dissolves in both acids and alkalis, forming beryllate salts $[	ext{Be(OH)}_4]^{2-}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A gas has molar volume $20\%$ smaller than ideal gas at same $T, P$. Compressibility factor $Z$ and dominant forces are:
questions.explanation: $Z = V_{\text{real}} / V_{\text{ideal}} = 0.8 < 1$. Attractive forces dominate causing negative deviation from ideality.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Anions A form HCP lattice and cations C occupy $75\%$ of octahedral voids. Formula of compound is:
questions.explanation: In HCP, number of octahedral voids equals number of anions $N$. Cations $C = 0.75 N = \frac{3}{4}N \implies \text{C}_{3/4}\text{A}_1 \implies \text{C}_3\text{A}_4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In which case is change in entropy NEGATIVE ($\Delta S < 0$)?
questions.explanation: Combining 2 free gaseous atoms into 1 diatomic molecule decreases disorder ($\Delta S < 0$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which spectral series of hydrogen atom emission falls in the VISIBLE spectrum region?
questions.explanation: Transitions ending at $n=2$ (Balmer series) emit photons in the visible spectrum ($400-700\text{ nm}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The chemical method used to remove TEMPORARY hardness of water is:
questions.explanation: Clark's method precipitates insoluble $\text{CaCO}_3$ and $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ by adding slaked lime.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following minerals is Malachite green copper ore?
questions.explanation: Malachite is basic copper carbonate $\text{CuCO}_3\cdot\text{Cu(OH)}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct order of basic strength of methyl-substituted amines in AQUEOUS solution is:
questions.explanation: Combined inductive effect, hydration enthalpy, and steric hindrance make dimethylamine ($2^\circ$) most basic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 called upon all nations:
questions.optionB: For conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilization of its benefits (Convention on Biological Diversity)
questions.optionC: To assess threat of invasive weeds
questions.explanation: Historic Earth Summit (CBD) aimed for biodiversity conservation and fair sharing of genetic benefits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Colostrum, the yellowish first milk secreted by mother, provides passive immunity to infants because it contains abundant:
questions.explanation: Colostrum is rich in secretory $\text{IgA}$ antibodies that protect the newborn gut mucosal barrier.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Grass leaves curl inwards during dry, hot weather to minimize water loss due to:
questions.optionB: Flaccidity of large empty bulliform / motor cells
questions.explanation: When bulliform cells lose water and become flaccid, leaf blade curls inward to reduce exposed surface area.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The shorter and longer arms of a submetacentric chromosome are designated as:
questions.explanation: The short arm is termed 'p' (petite) and the long arm is designated 'q'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) value of tripalmitin fat during cellular respiration is:
questions.explanation: $\text{RQ} = \frac{102\text{ CO}_2}{145\text{ O}_2} \approx 0.7$ for tripalmitin fatty acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a commercial blood cholesterol lowering statin produced by yeast Monascus purpureus?
questions.explanation: Statins competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase involved in cholesterol biosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Gastrointestinal Anatomy:
(a) Crypts of Lieberkühn, (b) Glisson's capsule, (c) Islets of Langerhans, (d) Brunner's glands
(i) Pancreas, (ii) Duodenum submucosa, (iii) Small intestine mucosa, (iv) Liver lobules
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Crypts = Intestine (iii), Glisson = Liver (iv), Islets = Pancreas (i), Brunner = Duodenum (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which is the MOST IMPORTANT cause driving animals and plants to extinction ('The Evil Quartet')?
questions.explanation: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the primary cause of global biodiversity loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which part of the human brain contains the thermoregulatory center controlling body temperature?
questions.explanation: Hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst, and endocrine homeostasis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Animal phyla exhibiting: (a) Organ system level, (b) Bilateral symmetry, (c) True coelom with metameric segmentation are:
questions.explanation: Annelids, Arthropods, and Chordates share true segmentation, bilateral symmetry, and organ-system organization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Correct sequential order of digestive organs in cockroach starting from mouth is:
questions.optionA: Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Crop $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
questions.optionB: Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Crop $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
questions.optionC: Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Crop $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
questions.optionD: Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Crop $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
questions.explanation: Food passes from pharynx through oesophagus into storage crop, muscular grinding gizzard, then ileum, colon, and rectum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which pair of gases contributes MOST ($>80\%$) to global warming greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: $\text{CO}_2$ contributes $\sim 60\%$ and $\text{CH}_4$ contributes $\sim 20\%$ to global greenhouse warming.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following muscular disorders is an INHERITED genetic disorder?
questions.explanation: Muscular dystrophy is a hereditary X-linked recessive disorder causing progressive muscle degeneration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Ciliated epithelial cells which move particles/mucus in a specific direction line the inner surface of:
questions.explanation: Ciliated columnar epithelium lines respiratory bronchioles and female fallopian tubes to propel mucus and ova.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Electrocardiogram (ECG) Waves:
(a) P-wave, (b) QRS complex, (c) T-wave, (d) Reduction in size of T-wave
(i) Depolarisation of ventricles, (ii) Repolarisation of ventricles, (iii) Coronary ischemia, (iv) Depolarisation of atria
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: P-wave = Atrial depolarisation (iv), QRS = Ventricular depolarisation (i), T-wave = Ventricular repolarisation (ii), Flattened T = Ischemia (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an IN-SITU biodiversity conservation method?
questions.explanation: Botanical gardens, zoological parks, and seed banks are ex-situ (off-site) conservation methods.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Newborn weight $2-5\text{ kg}$. $97\%$ infants between $3-3.3\text{ kg}$ survive, while weights $<2.5$ or $>4.5\text{ kg}$ die. This natural selection is:
questions.explanation: Selection against extreme phenotypes favoring intermediate mean birth weight is stabilizing selection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The correct sequential progression of cell cycle phases is:
questions.explanation: Interphase consists of Gap 1 ($G_1$), Synthesis ($S$), and Gap 2 ($G_2$), followed by Mitotic ($M$) division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: How do lipid-soluble STEROID hormones influence intracellular activities?
questions.optionB: Binding to intracellular receptors and forming hormone-receptor complexes on nuclear DNA
questions.explanation: Steroid hormones diffuse across cell membrane and bind nuclear receptors to regulate gene expression.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement about Lysosomes is NOT correct?
questions.optionB: Hydrolytic enzymes are active under acidic pH ($~5$)
questions.optionD: Lysosomes are formed directly by packaging in rough ER (Formed by Golgi apparatus packaging)
questions.explanation: Lysosomal enzymes synthesized by ER are packaged into functional lysosomes by Golgi cisternae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding post-fertilization changes in flowering plants is INCORRECT?
questions.optionC: Central cell develops into triploid endosperm
questions.optionD: Ovules develop into embryo sac (Ovules develop into seeds)
questions.explanation: Post-fertilization, ovules mature into seeds and the ovary develops into fruit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Concanavalin A isolated from Jack bean is categorized as a:
questions.explanation: Concanavalin A is a plant lectin (glycoprotein-binding protein).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which equipment is essential for large-scale industrial microbial culture and enzyme production?
questions.explanation: Bioreactors provide optimum aeration, temperature, pH, and nutrient conditions for high-volume culture.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Consider enzyme statements:
(A) Prosthetic group is a tightly bound organic/inorganic non-protein cofactor.
(B) Apoenzyme is the inactive protein component.
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: (A) is true. In statement (B), holoenzyme is complete active enzyme; apoenzyme is only the protein part.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Purine nitrogenous bases found in both DNA and RNA nucleic acids are:
questions.explanation: Adenine (A) and Guanine (G) are double-ring purines present in both DNA and RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Correct anatomical pathway for transport of sperm cells in human male reproductive system is:
questions.optionA: Testis $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vasa efferentia $\to$ Rete testis
questions.optionB: Seminiferous tubules $\to$ Rete testis $\to$ Vasa efferentia $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vas deferens $\to$ Ejaculatory duct $\to$ Urethra $\to$ Urethral meatus
questions.optionC: Seminiferous tubules $\to$ Vasa efferentia $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vas deferens
questions.optionD: Testis $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vasa efferentia $\to$ Inguinal canal
questions.explanation: Sperms travel: Seminiferous tubules $\to$ Rete testis $\to$ Vasa efferentia $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vas deferens $\to$ Ejaculatory duct $\to$ Urethra.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Hominid Ancestors with Cranial Capacities:
(a) Homo habilis, (b) Homo neanderthalensis, (c) Homo erectus, (d) Homo sapiens
(i) $900\text{ cc}$, (ii) $1400\text{ cc} / 1350\text{ cc}$, (iii) $650-800\text{ cc}$, (iv) $1400\text{ cc}$
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Homo habilis = $650-800\text{ cc}$ (iii), Neanderthal = $1400\text{ cc}$ (iv), Homo erectus = $900\text{ cc}$ (i), Homo sapiens = $1350-1400\text{ cc}$ (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: According to Hugo de Vries mutation theory, evolutionary mutations are:
questions.explanation: De Vries proposed single-step large mutations (saltation) that are random and directionless.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which pair of eukaryotic organelles does NOT contain any DNA genome?
questions.optionC: Lysosomes and Vacuoles (Single membrane organelles without DNA)
questions.explanation: Lysosomes and vacuoles lack DNA; mitochondria and chloroplasts contain circular semi-autonomous DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Asthma in urban areas causes respiratory wheezing primarily due to:
questions.optionB: Allergic inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles
questions.explanation: Asthma is an allergic condition causing bronchospasm and inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding sex determination:
questions.optionB: In male grasshoppers, $50\%$ of sperms have no sex chromosome (XO)
questions.optionC: In domesticated fowls, sex depends on sperm rather than egg (Female is heterogametic ZW)
questions.optionD: Human Y-chromosome is shorter than X
questions.explanation: In birds (fowls), females are heterogametic (ZW) producing Z and W eggs, so sex is determined by the ovum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: During recombinant DNA extraction, DNA spooling/precipitation is achieved by adding:
questions.explanation: Addition of ice-chilled ethanol precipitates purified DNA as delicate threads.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correct group of BIOCONTROL agents:
questions.explanation: Trichoderma controls root pathogens; Baculoviruses target arthropods; Bt controls insect larvae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding animal inbreeding:
questions.optionB: Inbreeding is essential to evolve purelines in cattle
questions.optionC: Inbreeding selects harmful recessive genes that reduce fertility (Inbreeding depression is caused by continuous close inbreeding)
questions.optionD: Inbreeding helps eliminate undesirable genes by exposing harmful recessives
questions.explanation: Close inbreeding exposes harmful recessive genes so they can be eliminated by selection; statement (c) misstates the role.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Microbes with Commercial Fermentation Products:
(a) Lactobacillus, (b) Saccharomyces cerevisiae, (c) Aspergillus niger, (d) Acetobacter aceti
(i) Cheese, (ii) Curd, (iii) Citric acid, (iv) Bread/Ethanol, (v) Acetic acid
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus = Curd (ii), Yeast = Bread (iv), Aspergillus = Citric (iii), Acetobacter = Acetic (v).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What is the direction of movement of sucrose/sugars in Phloem?
questions.explanation: Phloem transport is bi-directional depending on seasonal metabolic source-to-sink requirements.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Development of an embryo directly from unfertilized female gamete (ovum) is called:
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is development of an unfertilized egg into an individual (e.g. honeybee drones, rotifers, turkey).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Persistent, residual nucellus remaining in mature seeds (like black pepper and beet) is called:
questions.explanation: Perisperm is nutritive persistent maternal nucellus tissue outside the endosperm in seeds like Piper nigrum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A map unit (1 centiMorgan) on a chromosome represents:
questions.optionC: Distance between genes on chromosome representing $1\%$ recombination frequency
questions.explanation: Alfred Sturtevant defined $1\text{ cM}$ as $1\%$ frequency of genetic crossing over.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If cardiac output is $5\text{ L}$, end-diastolic volume is $100\text{ mL}$, and end-systolic volume is $50\text{ mL}$, heart rate is:
questions.explanation: $\text{Stroke Volume} = 100 - 50 = 50\text{ mL}$. $\text{Heart Rate} = \frac{\text{Cardiac Output}}{\text{Stroke Volume}} = \frac{5000\text{ mL}}{50\text{ mL}} = 100\text{ beats/min}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Thiobacillus denitrificans and Pseudomonas are bacteria helpful in:
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria convert soil nitrates back into molecular nitrogen gas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which factor is primarily responsible for producing hyperosmotic concentrated urine in mammalian nephrons?
questions.optionB: Maintaining hyperosmolarity gradient towards inner medullary interstitium by countercurrent multiplier
questions.explanation: Countercurrent mechanism in Henle's loop and vasa recta establishes medullary osmotic gradient ($300 \to 1200\text{ mOsm/L}$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding mitochondria is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: Outer membrane is permeable to monomers of nutrients
questions.optionB: Enzymes of electron transport chain are embedded in outer membrane (Embedded in inner mitochondrial membrane)
questions.optionC: Inner membrane is convoluted into cristae infoldings
questions.optionD: Mitochondrial matrix contains circular DNA and 70S ribosomes
questions.explanation: Complexes I through V of the electron transport system are localized in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Xylem vascular tissue translocates:
questions.optionC: Water, mineral salts and some organic nitrogen only
questions.optionD: Water, mineral salts, organic nitrogen compounds and plant hormones
questions.explanation: Xylem translocates water, inorganic minerals, amino acids, and root-synthesized phytohormones (cytokinins).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Cells in quiescent $G_0$ phase:
questions.optionA: Exit the cell cycle (remain metabolically active without division)
questions.explanation: Cells in $G_0$ have exited the active proliferative cycle but remain metabolically competent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement is NOT true about formation of Annual Rings in secondary xylem?
questions.optionA: Annual ring combines light springwood and dark autumnwood
questions.optionB: Differential cambial activity forms alternating light and dark bands
questions.optionC: Activity of vascular cambium responds to seasonal climatic variations
questions.optionD: Annual rings are not prominent in trees of temperate regions (Temperate trees have distinct annual rings)
questions.explanation: Temperate regions have sharp climatic seasons, producing prominent annual growth rings.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which ecological pyramid is generally INVERTED in nature?
questions.optionC: Pyramid of biomass in a forest
questions.optionD: Pyramid of biomass in sea / aquatic ecosystems
questions.explanation: Biomass of fishes far exceeds standing crop of short-lived phytoplankton in ocean ecosystems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Placentation where ovules develop on the inner wall or peripheral part of unilocular ovary (e.g. Mustard and Argemone) is:
questions.explanation: In parietal placentation, ovules attach to peripheral ovary walls, often with false septum replum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which international protocol was adopted in 1987 to reduce emissions of ozone depleting chlorofluorocarbons?
questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol (effective 1989) regulates global emission of ozone-depleting substances.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following contraceptive methods DO involve a hormonal mechanism of action?
questions.optionA: Lactational amenorrhea, Oral contraceptive pills, and Emergency contraceptives
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea (prolactin inhibition of GnRH), oral pills (progestins), and emergency pills are hormone-based.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If Tidal Volume $= 500\text{ mL}$, $\text{ERV} = 1000\text{ mL}$, $\text{RV} = 1200\text{ mL}$, what is Expiratory Capacity (EC)?
questions.explanation: $\text{Expiratory Capacity (EC)} = \text{TV} + \text{ERV} = 500 + 1000 = 1500\text{ mL}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What is the fate of the two male gametes discharged into the synergid during angiosperm double fertilization?
questions.optionA: One fuses with egg, other degenerates
questions.optionC: One fuses with egg, other fuses with synergid nucleus
questions.optionD: One fuses with egg (syngamy $\to$ zygote) and the other fuses with central cell polar nuclei (triple fusion $\to$ PEN)
questions.explanation: One sperm fuses with egg nucleus ($n+n=2n$) and second sperm fuses with diploid secondary nucleus ($n+2n=3n$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The organ of perception of photoperiodic light/dark cycle for floral induction in plants is:
questions.explanation: Leaves perceive light stimuli and generate florigen signal translocated to shoot apex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the correctly formatted binomial scientific name of Mango described by Carolus Linnaeus:
questions.explanation: Generic name capitalized, specific epithet in lowercase, followed by author citation in Roman: Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT statement describing Restriction Endonucleases:
questions.optionA: Cuts DNA at specific identified recognition sequence
questions.optionB: Binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only ONE of the two strands (Cuts BOTH strands of DNA duplex)
questions.optionC: Cleaves sugar-phosphate backbone at specific phosphodiester bonds
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cleave both strands of DNA double helix.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Retention of female gametophyte with developing young embryo on parent sporophyte (seed habit precursor) is first observed in:
questions.explanation: Heterosporous pteridophytes retain female gametophyte on sporophyte, an important evolutionary step towards seed habit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In Snapdragon (Antirrhinum), red ($RR$) crossed with white ($rr$) gives pink ($Rr$). In $F_2$, phenotypic ratio is $1:2:1$. Choose INCORRECT statement:
questions.optionA: This experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance
questions.optionB: Pink colour in $F_1$ is due to incomplete dominance
questions.optionC: Ratio of $F_2$ is $1/4\text{ Red} : 2/4\text{ Pink} : 1/4\text{ White}$
questions.optionD: Law of Segregation does not apply in this experiment (Law of Segregation is universally valid)
questions.explanation: Alleles segregate during gamete formation, so Mendel's Law of Segregation is fully upheld.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate in first irreversible step of glycolysis is catalyzed by:
questions.explanation: Hexokinase phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate by consuming ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The narcotic opioid drug 'Heroin' (Smack / diacetylmorphine) is synthesized by:
questions.optionB: Acetylation of morphine using acetic anhydride
questions.explanation: Diacetylation of morphine with acetic anhydride yields diacetylmorphine (heroin).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the HORMONE-RELEASING Intrauterine Devices (IUDs):
questions.explanation: Progestasert and LNG-20 release progesterone derivatives, making cervix hostile to sperm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: For gene with alleles $A$ and $a$, frequency of dominant allele $p(A) = 0.4$. Frequencies of $AA, Aa, aa$ in population are:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement is TRUE for Golden Rice genetically engineered crop?
questions.optionA: It is Vitamin A ($\beta$-carotene) enriched with genes from Daffodil (Narcissus) and Erwinia
questions.optionB: It is pest resistant with Bt toxin
questions.optionD: It has yellow grains from primitive rice variety
questions.explanation: Golden rice is biofortified with provitamin A ($\beta$-carotene) using phytoene synthase gene from daffodil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Pinus seeds cannot germinate and establish without fungal association because:
questions.optionB: It has an obligate symbiotic association with Mycorrhizae
questions.optionC: It has very hard seed coat
questions.explanation: Pinus roots lack root hairs and rely obligately on ectomycorrhizal fungi for water and phosphorus absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which feature of the genetic code allows human insulin gene to be accurately expressed in E. coli bacteria?
questions.optionC: Genetic code is nearly universal (same triplet codons code for same amino acids across species)
questions.explanation: Universality of genetic code enables heterologous gene expression in recombinant bacterial hosts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following Sexually Transmitted Infections is NOT completely curable?
questions.optionC: Genital herpes (along with Hepatitis B and HIV)
questions.explanation: HIV, Hepatitis-B, and Genital herpes infections cannot be completely cured.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.optionC: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat (Infective material is nucleic acid DNA/RNA)
questions.optionD: Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins
questions.explanation: Hershey-Chase proved genetic and infectious material of viruses is nucleic acid, not protein coat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Animals with Excretory / Anatomical Organs:
(a) Pila (Mollusca), (b) Bombyx (Arthropoda), (c) Pleurobrachia (Ctenophora), (d) Taenia (Platyhelminthes)
(i) Flame cells (Protonephridia), (ii) Comb plates, (iii) Radula rasper, (iv) Malpighian tubules
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Pila = Radula (iii), Bombyx = Malpighian tubules (iv), Pleurobrachia = Comb plates (ii), Taenia = Flame cells (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In Human Genome Project, Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to:
questions.optionA: All genes that are expressed as RNA transcripts (cDNA)
questions.explanation: ESTs identify all genes expressed as messenger RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement regarding Fungi is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: Morels and truffles are edible Ascomycete delicacies
questions.optionB: Claviceps purpurea produces ergot alkaloids and LSD precursor
questions.optionC: Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously
questions.optionD: Yeasts have long filamentous hyphal bodies (Yeasts are unicellular)
questions.explanation: Yeasts (Saccharomyces) are unicellular fungi, not filamentous mycelia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biological Interactions:
(a) Saprophyte, (b) Parasite, (c) Lichens, (d) Mycorrhiza
(i) Symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots, (ii) Decomposes dead organic matter, (iii) Living on/in living hosts, (iv) Symbiosis of algae and fungi
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Saprophyte = Dead matter (ii), Parasite = Living host (iii), Lichens = Algae+Fungi (iv), Mycorrhiza = Fungi+Roots (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which glucose transporter is INSULIN-DEPENDENT for glucose uptake into muscle and adipose tissue?
questions.explanation: GLUT4 is the insulin-sensitive facilitated glucose transporter expressed in skeletal muscle and adipose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which immune response is primarily responsible for graft / organ transplant rejection in humans?
questions.explanation: Cytotoxic T-lymphocytes (Cell-Mediated Immunity) recognize foreign HLA antigens and reject transplanted grafts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Artificial kidney (Haemodialysis) in renal failure patients may result in:
(a) Nitrogenous waste accumulation
(b) Non-elimination of potassium
(c) Reduced calcium absorption from GI tract (due to lack of calcitriol)
(d) Reduced RBC production (due to lack of erythropoietin)
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Damaged kidneys cannot activate Vitamin D (calcitriol) or produce erythropoietin, causing hypocalcemia and anaemia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is TRUE about the Cornea of the human eye?
questions.optionA: Cornea is external, transparent and protective covering of eye
questions.optionB: Cornea has dense connective tissue of elastin
questions.optionD: Cornea consists of dense matrix of collagen and is the most sensitive portion of eye
questions.explanation: Cornea is an avascular collagen-rich anterior transparent layer with dense sensory nerve endings (Official key: 4).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The use of recombination frequency between gene pairs to construct the first genetic map was done by:
questions.explanation: Alfred Sturtevant, student of T.H. Morgan, constructed the first chromosome gene map.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Genes of Lac Operon with Products:
(a) $i$ gene, (b) $z$ gene, (c) $a$ gene, (d) $y$ gene
(i) $\beta$-Galactosidase, (ii) Permease, (iii) Lac Repressor protein, (iv) Transacetylase
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: $i$ = Repressor (iii), $z$ = $\beta$-galactosidase (i), $a$ = Transacetylase (iv), $y$ = Permease (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which combination of plant hormones is applied to artificially induce synchronous flowering in Pineapple?
questions.explanation: Auxins and ethylene promote and synchronize flowering in pineapples throughout the year.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Mucus-secreting cells that protect mucosal lining of gastrointestinal tract from proteolytic enzymes are:
questions.explanation: Mucus secreted by goblet cells lubricates and protects gut lining from $\text{HCl}$ and pepsin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an effective fungal biocontrol agent for root-borne plant diseases?
questions.explanation: Free-living soil fungus Trichoderma is a potent biocontrol agent against fungal root pathogens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Phloem tissue in GYMNOSPERMS (like Pinus and Cycas) lacks:
questions.optionD: Both Sieve tubes and Companion cells (Possess sieve cells and albuminous cells instead)
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms have sieve cells and Strasburger/albuminous cells, lacking specialized sieve tube elements and companion cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Extrusion of the second polar body from the nucleus of the secondary oocyte occurs:
questions.optionA: After entry of sperm but before completion of fertilization / syngamy
questions.optionC: Before entry of sperm into ovum
questions.explanation: Sperm entry stimulates second meiotic division of oocyte, releasing second polar body prior to pronuclear fusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In mRNA $5'-\text{AACAGCGGUGCUAUU}-3'$, reading frame will NOT change (remain in-frame) upon:
questions.optionC: Insertion of A and G at 4th and 5th positions
questions.optionD: Deletion of complete triplet GGU from 7th, 8th and 9th positions
questions.explanation: Deleting or inserting multiples of 3 nucleotides (a whole codon) removes one amino acid without causing frameshift mutation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The cell theory aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' (all cells arise from pre-existing cells) was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Rudolf Virchow expanded Schleiden and Schwann's cell theory by establishing cellular biogenesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: What triggers the activation of inactive protoxin of Bacillus thuringiensis into active toxin in bollworm gut?
questions.optionC: Alkaline pH of the insect midgut
questions.explanation: Alkaline pH of insect midgut solubilizes crystalline endotoxin and activates it to create epithelial pores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the correct pair representing causative pathogen and confirmatory diagnostic test for Typhoid fever:
questions.explanation: Typhoid caused by Salmonella typhi is confirmed by serological Widal agglutination test.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Genetic disorder with masculine development, tall stature, gynecomastia and sterile male ($44 + \text{XXY}$) is:
questions.explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome results from sex-chromosomal aneuploidy XXY with 47 chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Polyblend, a fine recycled modified plastic powder developed by Ahmed Khan, is blended with bitumen for:
questions.explanation: Polyblend mixed with bitumen enhances water repellency and triples road life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The most appropriate method for long-term safe disposal of high-level nuclear waste is:
questions.optionD: Bury the shielded waste within deep shielded geological rock formations below Earth's surface (~500 m)
questions.explanation: Deep underground geological repository in pre-treated containers is the recommended nuclear disposal method.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Endocrine Hormones with Disorders:
(a) Insulin, (b) Thyroxin, (c) Corticoids, (d) Growth Hormone
(i) Addison's disease, (ii) Diabetes insipidus, (iii) Acromegaly, (iv) Goitre, (v) Diabetes mellitus
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Insulin = Diabetes mellitus (v), Thyroxin = Goitre (iv), Corticoids = Addison (i), GH = Acromegaly (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the CORRECT anatomical statement about human rib cage:
questions.optionB: 11th and 12th ribs connect to sternum via hyaline cartilage
questions.optionC: Each rib is attached to thoracic vertebrae and sternum
questions.optionD: There are 7 pairs of vertebrosternal (true) ribs, 3 pairs of vertebrochondral (false) ribs, and 2 pairs of vertebral (floating) ribs
questions.explanation: Ribs 1-7 are true ribs (vertebrosternal), ribs 8-10 are false ribs (vertebrochondral), ribs 11-12 are floating ribs (vertebral).
